# Reference: interface scripting
Load it for: making a GUI actually work: buttons that buy or equip, live currency labels, inventories that fill from data, notifications, mobile and gamepad input

The `gui` reference builds how an interface looks. This one covers the LocalScripts and remotes behind it. Only add this logic when the user wants a working system, not the interface alone.

## Structure
- ScreenGuis live in `StarterGui` and are cloned into each player's `PlayerGui` on spawn. Set `ResetOnSpawn = false` on anything that should keep its state through death, and handle `CharacterAdded` yourself.
- One controller LocalScript per screen (or one for the whole HUD), under the ScreenGui or in `StarterPlayerScripts`. Not a script inside every button.
- The client never decides outcomes. Buttons send a request; the server answers; the client draws the answer.
- Interfaces built with the Lurong Kit already open, close and switch tabs through `LurongAction` attributes. Do not rewrite that; add your logic beside it by finding buttons by name.

## Wiring a button
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local gui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui"):WaitForChild("ShopGui")
local buy = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes"):WaitForChild("BuyItem")

local busy = false
local function onBuy(itemId: string, button: GuiButton)
	if busy then return end
	busy = true
	local ok, reason = buy:InvokeServer(itemId)
	busy = false
	if not ok then notify(reason or "Could not buy that") end
end
```
- Use `Activated`, not `MouseButton1Click`: it fires for mouse, touch and gamepad.
- `InvokeServer` yields; guard against double clicks with a flag, and wrap in `pcall` if the server handler can error.

## Showing live values
- Currency and stats: listen, do not poll.
```lua
local coins = player:WaitForChild("leaderstats"):WaitForChild("Coins")
local function show() label.Text = format(coins.Value) end
coins:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Value"):Connect(show)
show()
```
- Attributes: `player:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Coins")`.
- Big state (inventory): the server sends a snapshot once and small updates after; the client keeps a local copy and redraws only what changed.
- Number formatting: 1,234 with separators below a million; 1.2M, 3.4B, 5.6T above. Put the formatter in one shared module.

## Lists that fill from data
- Keep one hidden **template** row or tile in the ScreenGui. For each entry: `Clone`, fill the labels, set a `LayoutOrder`, parent it to the ScrollingFrame, connect its button. Never build rows property by property in code.
- Clear old rows before refilling (skip the template and the layout object). Disconnect their connections or they leak; cloning plus `Destroy` handles this if connections are made on the clone's own descendants.
- `ScrollingFrame.AutomaticCanvasSize = Y` with `CanvasSize` zero, so the list scrolls correctly.
- For hundreds of entries, show a page at a time.

## Motion
- Open: scale from 0.9 to 1 and fade in over 0.2 s (`TweenService`, `Back`/`Quad` Out) using a `UIScale`; close faster than open. Kit windows already do this.
- Hover and press feedback on every button. Never block input with a tween that has no end state.

## Screen sizes and input
- Test at phone size (roughly 812x375) and desktop. Kit interfaces scale themselves; for your own, use scale-based sizes plus `UIAspectRatioConstraint`, and `UITextSizeConstraint` or `TextScaled` for text.
- Minimum touch target about 44x44 pixels.
- `GuiService:GetGuiInset()` and `ScreenGui.IgnoreGuiInset` for the top bar area. Leave the default jump button and thumbstick area free on mobile.
- Detect touch with `UserInputService.TouchEnabled` only to adapt layout, not to gate features.
- Keyboard shortcuts: `ContextActionService:BindAction` so they also get a mobile button if wanted, and unbind when the screen closes.
- Gamepad: set `GuiService.SelectedObject` when a menu opens so it can be navigated.

## Notifications
- One `Notify` RemoteEvent, one client function that shows a toast: clone a template, slide in, hold 2 to 3 s, slide out, destroy. Queue or stack them; never overlap.
- `StarterGui:SetCore("SendNotification", {...})` is fine for simple cases; wrap in `pcall` and retry, it is not ready at once.

## Billboards and world UI
- `BillboardGui` for name tags and health bars above heads (`AlwaysOnTop`, `MaxDistance`, `StudsOffset`); parent to the character's head on the server or in `StarterCharacterScripts`.
- `SurfaceGui` for boards and screens; parent it to `PlayerGui` with its `Adornee` set when its buttons must be clickable.
- `ProximityPrompt` for "press E" interactions; handle `Triggered` on the server.

## Hiding the defaults
- `StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, false)` and similar, in a LocalScript, only when the user asks.

## Common faults
- Editing `StarterGui` at runtime and expecting players to see it: they see their own copy in `PlayerGui`.
- `WaitForChild` missing on the client, so the script errors before the GUI exists.
- A LocalScript in `ServerScriptService` or a Script expecting `LocalPlayer`: neither runs.
- ZIndex fights: set `ZIndexBehavior = Sibling` and order by hierarchy.
- Text that overflows on phones: constrain it and test at phone size.
